text:
Here are the strongest open-ear options for running right now, based on recent reviews from Runner's World, WIRED, SoundGuys, and RTINGS.

**1. Bose Ultra Open Earbuds: best overall (clip-on)**
- Runner's World picks these as its overall winner. WIRED calls them the best sound in clip-on open earbuds and prefers their physical buttons for running. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- Runner's World lists them at $199, down from $299. WIRED lists $199 at Bose.
- Drawbacks: they're expensive, rated IPX4, and get about 7 hours per charge. Runner's World also says Bose is releasing a new pair soon.

**2. Shokz OpenRun Pro 2: best bone conduction**
- It has more bass than the older OpenRun, uses USB-C, and gets about 12 hours of battery life. WIRED rates it 8/10 and says the trade-off is some lost clarity. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)
- Listed at $180, and WIRED shows $125 at REI and Best Buy.
- Drawbacks: a high ponytail or hood can interfere with the band, and it's IP55 rather than fully waterproof. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**3. Shokz OpenDots 2: best for long runs**
- Runner's World and WIRED both recommend these. They offer 10 hours of battery life and 40 hours with the case. WIRED cites an IP57 rating. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- Listed at $200.
- Drawback: no noise cancellation, and volume could be louder.

**4. Soundcore AeroFit 2: best value hook-style pick**
- Soundcore's open-ear hook design has 10 hours per bud and 42 hours with the case, and it supports LDAC on Android. SoundGuys named it its best budget pick. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- Prices differ by source. SoundGuys lists $79.99 at Amazon. Dealectric lists $129.99 at Soundcore's US store, and a code (AFSC20) for 20% off brought it to about $104 when tested on 2026-10-22. The code isn't valid on sale items and expires 2026-12-31. Checkout has the final say on price.
- Disclosure: the Dealectric page is an affiliate link. It earns a commission if you buy, at no extra cost to you. [Buy via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2) · [Product page](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2)

**5. Budget: JLab Flex Open**
- Runner's World calls these the best budget pick, at about $40 to $50. They're comfortable and loud enough for most settings, but the sound is weaker than pricier pairs. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Also worth a look: Nothing Ear (Open)**
- SoundGuys names it its best pick for running. It's listed at $99 on sale (MSRP $149) with IP54 protection. [SoundGuys workout list](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)

**My suggestion:** For the best all-around experience, go with the Bose Ultra Open if the budget allows. If you want the most bass, choose the OpenRun Pro 2. For a lower price, try the AeroFit 2 or JLab Flex Open.

**Safety note:** Open-ear designs leak sound and don't block noise. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic and people around you.
